Aspecto verbal: por que os verbos vêm em: Verbal aspect: why verbs come in pairs
A promessa cumprida: por que quase todo: A promise kept: why does almost every Russian verb come in a pair? In earlier lessons and vocabulary lists you noticed that almost all Russian verbs appear as a couple: де́лать / сде́лать (to do), чита́ть / прочита́ть (to read), писа́ть / написа́ть (to write), покупа́ть / купи́ть (to buy). The time has come to master this Russian superpower: verbal aspect (Вид глаго́ла). English has a dozen verb tenses ("I read", "I was reading", "I have read", "I had read"...). Russian has only three tenses (past, present and future), but it looks at any action through two different lenses. • 1. Imperfective (НСВ — Несоверше́нный вид) = THE FILM (process, routine, duration). It focuses on the action happening, repeating every day or lasting for a while, whether or not it finished. It corresponds to our "I was reading / I used to read / I read every day". • 2. Perfective (СВ — Соверше́нный вид) = THE PHOTOGRAPH (a single, completed result). It focuses on the end point, the mission accomplished, the finished result of one single occasion. It corresponds to our "I read the whole book / I have written the letter / I bought the ticket". The Compass: imperfective (НСВ) versus perfective (СВ). The big trick of the simple future (perfective): the perfective verb (сде́лать, прочита́ть, написа́ть, купи́ть) has no present. So when you apply the present-tense scissors to it, the result means COMPLETED FUTURE (and it never uses бу́ду!). де́лать (НСВ): я де́лаю (I do / am doing now) · я бу́ду де́лать (I will be doing / working on it). сде́лать (СВ): я сде́лаю (I will do it / I will get it done!) · ты сде́лаешь · он сде́лает.

Em russo, quase todo verbo tem DOIS infi: In Russian, almost every verb has TWO infinitives, called aspects. The imperfective looks at the action as a process, habit or repetition: «Я читал книгу» = I was reading a book (perhaps without finishing it). The perfective looks at the action as a whole, completed, with a result: «Я прочитал книгу» = I read the book to the end. English shows the same idea in the difference between "I was reading" and "I read it through" / "I finished reading". Guiding question: does the process or habit matter (imperfective), or the completed result (perfective)? The perfective is conjugated like any verb (1st or 2nd conjugation) and is often formed with a PREFIX: делать → сделать. Attention: the perfective has no present tense; its present-looking forms mean the future (next lesson). So when you study a verb, always study the pair: imperfective / perfective.

O jeito mais comum de formar o perfectiv: The most common way to form the perfective is to add a prefix to the imperfective. The most frequent ones: с- (делать → сделать), про- (читать → прочитать), на- (писать → написать), по- (смотреть → посмотреть), при- (готовить → приготовить), вы- (учить → выучить), у- (видеть → увидеть). Other pairs change the ending: покупать → купить, отвечать → ответить. Once formed, the perfective is conjugated like any verb; in the past: прочитал, прочитала, прочитали.
